name: The Cape Winelands
region: Western Cape, east of Cape Town
tagline: White Cape Dutch manor houses in oak-lined valleys, vineyards beneath jagged mountains and long lunches with award-winning wine, an hour from Cape Town.
highlight: A long lunch on a wine estate terrace, with a chilled chenin blanc and vineyards stretching to the mountains.
shortDescription: The heart of South African wine: Stellenbosch, Franschhoek, Paarl and Constantia, with historic estates, Cape Dutch architecture, food, art and superb scenery.
metaDescription: A Cape Winelands travel guide: Stellenbosch, Franschhoek, Paarl and Constantia, Cape Dutch estates, Pinotage and Chenin Blanc, the Wine Tram, Babylonstoren, best time, how to get there and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: Cape Town International (CPT), about 45 minutes to Stellenbosch
knownFor: Wine, Cape Dutch architecture, food, mountains
goodFor: Wine, food, scenery, cycling, romantic breaks

image.alt: Rows of vines in a Winelands vineyard beneath a mountain near Paarl

intro: South Africa has been making wine since 1659, when the first Cape vintage was pressed by the colony's Dutch founder, Jan van Riebeeck. The most important regions are in the mountain-ringed valleys east of Cape Town, where warm, dry summers and cool sea breezes are ideal for grapes. The area, called the Cape Winelands, includes the university town of Stellenbosch, the French-influenced village of Franschhoek, the larger town of Paarl, and the historic estates of Constantia on the edge of Cape Town.

The estates are as beautiful as the wine. Many are grouped around white, gabled Cape Dutch manor houses, some dating from the 17th and 18th centuries, with oaks, rose gardens and vineyards against a backdrop of dramatic mountains. Wine tasting is often paired with food, and restaurants in the region rank among the best in the country. The Cape's signature grapes include Chenin Blanc, Pinotage, a local cross, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah.

Wine tourism is well organised, with tasting rooms, tours, a Wine Tram in Franschhoek and cycling routes. It is close enough to Cape Town for a day trip, but a night or two is better, particularly in Franschhoek or Stellenbosch, where a stay on a vineyard estate is part of the experience.

whyVisit.intro: The Winelands combine some of the most beautiful landscapes in South Africa with excellent wine and food.

points.title: World-class wine
points.text: Estates producing Chenin Blanc, Pinotage, Cabernet and more, with tastings for all levels.

points.title: Superb scenery
points.text: Vineyards and mountains, with oak-lined roads and Cape Dutch buildings.

points.title: Fine dining
points.text: Restaurants and farm-to-table lunches at estates.

points.title: History
points.text: Stellenbosch, South Africa's second-oldest town, and Franschhoek's Huguenot heritage.

points.title: Easy access
points.text: About 45 minutes from Cape Town's airport.

attractionsIntro: Give each town a day, or combine them into a tour.

attractions.name: Stellenbosch

image.alt: Oak trees lining Dorp Street in Stellenbosch with historic houses

attractions.text: A university town founded in 1679, with oak-lined streets, Cape Dutch houses and museums, surrounded by more than 100 wine estates.
attractions.tip: Walk Dorp Street, and book a tasting.

attractions.name: Franschhoek

image.file: File:Huguenot Memorial Museum, Franschhoek, Western Cape, South Africa (20319433219).jpg
image.alt: The Huguenot Memorial and museum in Franschhoek with mountains behind

attractions.text: A village settled by French Huguenots in 1688, now known as the country's food and wine capital, with a memorial museum, boutiques and top restaurants.

attractions.name: Paarl

image.alt: Bunches of grapes ripening on vines in Paarl

attractions.text: A long town below a granite dome, with old estates, the Afrikaans Language Monument and a wine route.

attractions.name: Babylonstoren

image.alt: The gardens and Cape Dutch buildings at Babylonstoren farm

attractions.text: A farm and estate near Franschhoek with a huge kitchen garden, restaurants and a hotel in Cape Dutch buildings.

attractions.name: Groot Constantia

image.alt: The white Cape Dutch manor house at Groot Constantia wine estate

attractions.text: South Africa's oldest wine estate, founded in 1685, in Constantia on the edge of Cape Town, with a museum and tastings.

attractions.name: Cape Dutch estates
attractions.text: Manor houses such as Boschendal, Vergelegen and others, with tours, gardens and restaurants.

thingsToDoIntro: Wine, food and scenery make up the days.

thingsToDo.title: Taste wine at several estates
thingsToDo.text: Visit three or four, with a lunch break.
thingsToDo.tip: Book in advance and hire a driver.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the Franschhoek Wine Tram
thingsToDo.text: A hop-on hop-off tram and bus that links estates.

thingsToDo.title: Cycle through the vines
thingsToDo.text: Quiet roads and tracks link estates.

thingsToDo.title: Have a farm-to-table lunch
thingsToDo.text: Many estates serve seasonal menus with wine pairings.

thingsToDo.title: Hike in the mountains
thingsToDo.text: Trails in the Jonkershoek or Franschhoek mountains.

thingsToDo.title: Visit an art gallery or craft market
thingsToDo.text: Stellenbosch and Franschhoek have galleries and markets.

foodIntro: The Winelands' food is estate-led, with produce from farms and gardens and a mix of Cape traditions.

foods.name: Chenin Blanc
foods.text: The Cape's signature white, in styles from fresh to oaked.

foods.name: Pinotage
foods.text: A South African red, a cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault.

foods.name: Cape Winelands cuisine
foods.text: Modern dishes with local ingredients, such as springbok, trout and fruit.

foods.name: Cheese and olive oil
foods.text: Artisan cheese, olives and preserves at farm shops.

accommodation.intro: Stay on an estate or in a small town.

gettingThere.intro: The Winelands are 45 to 75 km from Cape Town.

options.text: About 45 minutes to Stellenbosch, 1 hour to Franschhoek, 50 minutes to Paarl.
Day tours from Cape Town are widely available.
options.detail: Best if you plan to drink.

gettingAround.intro: A driver or a tour is the easiest way to taste wine.

bestTime.headline: November–April
bestTime.summary: The Winelands have hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters.

seasons.text: Hot, sunny and green, with alfresco lunches.
Harvest season, golden vines and pleasant weather.
Cool and wet, with fires and low prices.

bestTime.avoid: The hottest days of January, and busy Easter and Christmas periods.

days.title: Stellenbosch
days.afternoon: Two estates and a long lunch.

tipsIntro: A few tips make wine touring better.
tips: Book tastings and lunches in advance.
Hire a driver or take a tour. Do not drink and drive.
Visit two or three estates a day, not more.
Ask about cellar tours and pairings.
Try wines you don't know, such as Chenin Blanc and Pinotage.
Wear sun protection and comfortable shoes.

faq.q: How many days do you need in the Winelands?
faq.a: Two or three days. A day trip from Cape Town is also possible.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?

faq.a: Franschhoek for food and charm, Stellenbosch for variety, and Paarl for a quieter feel.
It is strongly recommended if you plan to drink.

faq.q: What wine is South Africa known for?
faq.a: Chenin Blanc, Pinotage, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah.
Tastings are inexpensive, and wine and food are good value.
